subject: DPA execution & subprocessor notification — SaaSCo procurement request
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@saasco.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: procurement@saasco.com
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial DPA & Subprocessor list — Redwood

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the call this morning. Procurement has reviewed the standard DPA you provided and we'd like to confirm a couple items before we sign:

- We need a 30-day prior notice for any additions to the subprocessor list (our security policy requires 30 days for review).
- Please confirm whether Redwood supports EU->US transfer mechanisms in the DPA (we're seeing references to standard contractual clauses in section 5).
- Can you share an updated redline with the proposed change to the objection window and any DocuSign-ready execution package?

Attached is SaaSCo's subprocessor checklist and a summary of our legal team's redlines. If you can get the updated DPA by EOD tomorrow, procurement can route for signature.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Torres
Head of Procurement | SaaSCo Ltd
elena.torres@saasco.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: SaaSCo-Subprocessor-List-20260901.pdf

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@saasco.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.inference.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.inference.com>, priyom_das <priyom@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial DPA & Subprocessor list — Redwood

Elena —

Appreciate the clear asks and the checklist. Quick answers up front:
- We can accommodate a 30-day notification window for new subprocessors for enterprise (Reserved) customers. For hosted customers we default to a 14-day notice but we can make a contract-specific exception.
- The DPA references SCCs for EU transfers; we also support customer-specific transfer mechanisms (e.g., EU SCCs + binding addendum). Happy to add explicit language stating the transfer mechanisms we rely on.

I've attached an internal redline that (a) expands the notification window to 30 days for your account, (b) adds a callout in section 5 about transfer mechanisms, and (c) proposes language for how objection rights will work (escalation timeline + remediation). Please review.

We can send the DocuSign envelope once you confirm the redline. Do you want Redwood to initiate e-sign, or would you prefer legal to send the envelope from SaaSCo's side?

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.inference.com

Attachment: Redwood_DPA_redline_20260902.docx

From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@saasco.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: procurement@saasco.com, Vendor Legal <legal@saasco.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial DPA & Subprocessor list — Redwood

On Wed, Sep 02, 2026 at 11:03, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference.com> wrote:
> I've attached an internal redline that (a) expands the notification window to 30 days for your account...

Thanks, Rishi. Couple follow-ups from our legal team:

- The objection process text looks reasonable but we need a firm SLA for Redwood's response to objections (they're asking for a 5-business-day acknowledgement and a 20-business-day remediation plan or mitigation alternative).
- For the execution flow — procurement prefers SaaSCo to originate the DocuSign envelope when vendor redlines are included, so our legal can validate the final copy before e-sign.

If Redwood is comfortable with the 5/20 timelines, procurement will confirm and we can circulate the final DPA for signature.

Best,
Elena

Attachment: SaaSCo-Subprocessor-List-20260901.pdf (re-sent)

From: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.inference.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@saasco.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.inference.com>, priyom_das <priyom@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial DPA & Subprocessor list — Redwood

Elena,

Thanks for the feedback and for the preference on DocuSign origination. We can accept the 5-business-day acknowledgement + 20-business-day remediation plan timeline for SaaSCo. We'll fold that into the objection process clause and add a short operational note in the console that will trigger an internal ticket when SaaSCo objects to a subprocessor addition — that should tighten the remediation cadence.

A few clarifications:
- The 30-day notice will apply to new subprocessor additions that entail access to production data. Minor service-level changes (non-data-processing infra, telemetry collectors with no PII) will keep the 14-day window unless explicitly listed.
- We'll include an appendix in the DPA listing current subprocessors and a commitment to notify via the contract email address.

If SaaSCo will originate the DocuSign envelope, please send the final redline by end of day and copy legal@redwood.inference.com so our GC team can give a last-minute check before countersign.

Cheers,
Laura Bennett
VP, Security & Trust | Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.inference.com

---
Laura Bennett
VP, Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

Laura —

That all sounds workable. We will originate the DocuSign envelope after legal incorporates the 5/20 clause and the narrow definition around "production data" for the 30-day rule. Expect a finalized redline from Vendor Legal this morning. Once we receive the redline we'll upload to DocuSign and send a link to both signatories.

Two quick asks for your operations team so the transition is smooth:
1) Please send the current subprocessor appendix as a PDF (we need the static list for our compliance artifact repository).
2) Can you provide a point of contact for the notification mailbox (who receives the automated notice)?

Thanks again — looking forward to wrapping this up.

Elena
